issues.body: ReleaseLaneSafeTests still proves guard coverage with `assertIn(Path(entry).name, guard.read_text(...))`, and its discovery sweep uses the same substring criterion. `test_release_publish_guard.py` structurally reads release-plz.yml and release.yml, but its publish.yml occurrences are prose or assertion messages; it does not open or parse publish.yml. The REQUIRED_GUARDS entry for publish.yml therefore passes without validating any publish.yml invariant, so edits to that workflow can skip the Rust matrix while receiving no concrete guard promised by the carve-out.
issues.fix_hint: Either remove .github/workflows/publish.yml from _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE, or add a non-selector-gated guard that opens/parses publish.yml and asserts its load-bearing invariants. Make this audit verify a concrete read/parse relationship rather than a filename substring, and add a mutation test demonstrating that a meaningful publish.yml defect causes the guard to fail.
issues.title: publish.yml guard validation remains vacuous

verdict.summary: The round-4 major finding remains unresolved. The new audit still treats a raw filename substring as proof that a guard reads and validates a workflow. In the checked-out head, test_release_publish_guard.py defines and structurally parses release-plz.yml and release.yml, but publish.yml appears only in prose/messages; nevertheless REQUIRED_GUARDS maps publish.yml to that test, and both the explicit audit and discovery sweep accept those mentions. Thus arbitrary publish.yml changes are classified orchestration-only without a real validating guard, contrary to the documented second obligation. Because this is materially the same major soundness hole as round 4, progress is stagnant.
